description: Terminal precision: each scenario is N identical steps run through each library in its native representation for several inputs, against the same loop in exact arithmetic (mpmath, 200 digits), twice: from the exact parameters (digits) and from the parameters as the library received them (digitsFormat). See methodology.

versions.maker: dss pot.sol rpow via solady v0.1.26

methodology.truth: For every scenario, input and N the same loop is run in exact real arithmetic with mpmath at 300 decimal digits (scripts/ladder/ladder.py), from the exact rational parameters in scenarios.json. Closed forms are used where the loop has one (compounding, the cumulative product, the geometric mean, the round trip, per-second and continuous accrual, the option walk and the decay); the bonding curve, the amortising loan and the Black-Scholes chain are stepped.
methodology.rounding: Each library receives the parameters floored into its own representation (2^-128, 2^-64, 10^-18 or 10^-27 units, or the nearest float for ABDKMathQuad and FP256; scripts/ladder/inputs.json). truthFormat is the exact loop started from those floored parameters, so digitsFormat measures the library's arithmetic alone, while digits measures what a protocol sees: the format's rounding of the inputs plus the arithmetic.
methodology.digits: digits = floor(-log10 |v - t| / |t|), the number of correct leading significant digits by relative error, capped at 100, which is reported as exact. It is not a string comparison: a value can be correct to 36 digits while its 37th printed digit happens to agree with the truth, or while a carry makes the printed prefix differ earlier.
methodology.agree: agree is the count of leading significant digits of the printed value (42 significant digits) that are literally equal to the printed truth. The demo page colours the rest of the value with it. It is a reading aid, not a measurement: a carry across 0.999… / 1.000… gives 0.
methodology.gas: gasTotal is measured inside the adapter around the scenario function (the parameter reads and the loop), after the runner has warmed the adapter and the FP127 object, so the call into the adapter and the ABI decoding are excluded. The FP127 (deployed) form includes one staticcall per op; FP127Lib and the other libraries are internal calls. Aave, Morpho and Maker answer only the accrual scenarios their models describe and report Unsupported elsewhere, which the tables show as a revert. gasPerStep = gasTotal / N. Reverted cells carry no gas.
methodology.live: LadderRunner.run(scenario, form, n, p) on Sepolia executes any cell with one eth_call and returns (ok, raw, reason, gasPerStep, gasTotal). scripts/ladder/livecap.py sends every cell's floored parameters p and compares the returned raw word with the committed one bit for bit (or the revert selector for a reverted cell). liveMaxN is the largest N per form the public RPC completed within its gas limit, measured by scripts/ladder/livecap.py.
methodology.reproduce: make ladder regenerates ladder.json and ladder.md from the Foundry harness (test/ladder/Ladder.t.sol) and this script; make ladder-check fails CI when the committed dataset differs. Versions of every library and of forge are recorded in the dataset.

scenarios.title: Continuous accrual
scenarios.result: balance after N days of continuous accrual
scenarios.why: How Aave and Morpho accrue: the ideal is e^(rate * time), and both ship a three-term expansion of it (1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6), which Aave notes 'slightly underpays liquidity providers and undercharges borrowers'. Every library is judged against the exponential it approximates. The step here is one accrual spanning N days, which is what a market that nobody touched for N days computes on its next interaction; the expansion's error is x^4/24 with x = rate * years, so it is invisible at daily updates and the whole story at a year or more. Morpho holds the rate per second in WAD (1,585,489,599 wei at 5% APR), ten significant digits before any arithmetic; both digit counts show that loss, since the format truth is built from the annual rate the other libraries receive.
